testName: Air Brakes Test #1 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What should you do if the low pressure warning light comes on while driving?

options.text: Brakes will only work if there is enough air in the tanks.
You can brake 14 times before the air runs out.
Drive normally and check the brakes later.
Keep driving but turn on hazard lights to warn others.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brakes will only work if there is enough air in the tanks.
questions.explanation: When the low air pressure warning light comes on, stop and park safely as soon as possible. Your brakes will only work as long as air remains in the tanks.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system, what is separate?

options.text: Each system has its own air tanks, hoses, and lines.
The systems share air tanks but have separate hoses and lines.
Each system uses the same lines and hoses.
One main system and one backup system ready if the first fails.

questions.correctAnswerText: Each system has its own air tanks, hoses, and lines.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate brake systems. They share one set of brake controls, but each has its own air tanks, hoses, and lines.

questions.question: If the low pressure warning signal turns on while you are driving, what should you do?

options.text: Continue driving normally.
Exit the road and park as soon as safely possible.
Stop and park right away where you are.
Turn on hazard lights and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Exit the road and park as soon as safely possible.
questions.explanation: When the low pressure warning signal comes on, exit the road safely and park your vehicle. If air pressure gets too low, your brakes will not work well enough to stop safely.

questions.question: If the spring brakes are on, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Use the brake pedal.
Press the accelerator.
Turn the steering wheel.
Be careful because the brakes may fail.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: Do not use the brake pedal when spring brakes are on. Using both at the same time can damage the brakes.

questions.question: Braking mechanisms are located ____ a brake drum.

options.text: Outside
Inside
Next to
On top of

questions.correctAnswerText: Inside
questions.explanation: Drum brakes are attached to the wheels on the axles. The parts that stop the vehicle are found inside the brake drum.

questions.question: What does the air compressor governor control?

options.text: When the air compressor pumps air into the air storage tanks.
How quickly air leaves the air storage tanks.
The temperature of air entering the air storage tanks.
The temperature of air leaving the air storage tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the air compressor pumps air into the air storage tanks.
questions.explanation: The air compressor governor controls when the air compressor pumps air into the air storage tanks.

questions.question: When do brakes fade?

options.text: When brakes are not used often enough.
When brakes overheat.
When brakes are too cold.
When brakes are wet.

questions.correctAnswerText: When brakes overheat.
questions.explanation: Using brakes too much causes them to overheat and become less effective. This is called brake fading.

questions.question: What is the purpose of anti-lock brakes?

options.text: Prevent wheels from locking up.
Lock up the front wheels.
Stop a vehicle from accelerating uphill.
Stop a vehicle from accelerating downhill.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevent wheels from locking up.
questions.explanation: Anti-lock brakes (ABS) prevent the wheels from locking up when you brake hard.

questions.question: When the brake pedal is pressed and the S-cam turns, what happens?

options.text: The S-cam presses brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum.
The S-cam tightens the brake drum onto the axle.
The S-cam presses brake lining against the wheel.
The S-cam releases air from the air tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: The S-cam presses brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum.
questions.explanation: When you press the brake pedal and the S-cam turns, it presses the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum. This friction slows the vehicle.

questions.question: If the spring brakes are on, what should you never do?

options.text: Push down the brake pedal.
Open the hood.
Release air from the air storage tanks.
Open the cab door.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push down the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: Never push the brake pedal when spring brakes are on. Using both at the same time can damage the brakes.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system, what do both systems share?

options.text: Air tanks.
Hoses.
Air lines.
An air compressor.

questions.correctAnswerText: An air compressor.
questions.explanation: Both systems in a dual air brake system share one air compressor. If the compressor breaks, neither system will work.

questions.question: What happens if you press and release the brake pedal too often?

options.text: Air escapes faster than the compressor can replace it.
More air is added to the braking system.
The brake pedal becomes more sensitive.
A loud noise is created.

questions.correctAnswerText: Air escapes faster than the compressor can replace it.
questions.explanation: Pressing and releasing the brake pedal too often causes air to escape from the braking system faster than the compressor can refill it.

questions.question: What happens if brake pads rub against brake drums and create too much heat?

options.text: The brakes will stick.
The brakes will become extra sensitive.
The brakes may stop working.
The air compressor will turn on to cool the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: The brakes may stop working.
questions.explanation: When brakes overheat from too much use, they become less effective. The heat causes expansion and chemical changes that make the brakes stop working. This is called "brake fade."

questions.question: What should you do when driving down a steep hill?

options.text: Use the air brakes.
Shift into a low gear, then use brakes to help slow the engine's braking effect.
Downshift continuously instead of using the brakes.
Drive on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift into a low gear, then use brakes to help slow the engine's braking effect.
questions.explanation: On a hill, let the engine do most of the braking by shifting to a low gear before you start down. Use the brakes only when you need extra stopping power.

questions.question: What should you do before starting down a hill?

options.text: Speed up.
Shift into a high gear.
Honk your horn.
Shift into a low gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift into a low gear.
questions.explanation: Before going down a hill, shift into a low gear. Gravity will make your vehicle go faster as you travel downhill.

questions.question: How often should an alcohol evaporator be checked and filled in cold weather?

options.text: Once a week.
Every day.
Every hour.
Once a month.

questions.correctAnswerText: Every day.
questions.explanation: An alcohol evaporator prevents ice from building up in an air brake system. In cold weather, check and refill it every day.

questions.question: At 55 mph on dry pavement, how much distance does brake lag add to your stopping distance?

options.text: 32 feet
15 feet
50 feet
10 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: 32 feet
questions.explanation: Total stopping distance includes perception distance, reaction distance, brake lag distance, and braking distance. At 55 mph on dry pavement, brake lag adds about 32 feet.

questions.question: What does a one-way check valve do?

options.text: Drains water and compressor oil from the air tanks.
Stops air from escaping if the air compressor leaks.
Turns on the emergency brakes when there is a leak.
Holds the spring brakes in place until they are used.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stops air from escaping if the air compressor leaks.
questions.explanation: A one-way check valve is installed between the air compressor and the main storage tank. It stops air from leaking out of the system if the compressor breaks.

questions.question: Before driving, when should spring brakes come on automatically?

options.text: When air pressure falls below 45 psi.
When air pressure falls below 20 psi.
When driving downhill.
When driving uphill.

questions.correctAnswerText: When air pressure falls below 45 psi.
questions.explanation: Test that spring brakes activate automatically when air pressure drops to between 20 and 45 psi. Block the wheels and release air by pressing the brake pedal. When pressure gets low, the parking brake valve will pop out and spring brakes will activate.

questions.question: What do air storage tanks do?

options.text: Hold air for only one braking cycle.
Hold enough air to use the brakes several times if the compressor stops working.
Hold air only during an emergency.
Hold enough air for more than 1,000 braking cycles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold enough air to use the brakes several times if the compressor stops working.
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks hold enough air so you can brake several times even if the compressor stops working.

questions.question: When should service brakes be tested?

options.text: Once a month.
Only by a trained mechanic.
Before every trip.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before every trip.
questions.explanation: Always test your service brakes before you drive. This helps you find problems before you need to brake on the road.

questions.question: How can you check if a trailer has ABS?

options.text: Look under the trailer for wheel speed sensors near the back of the brakes.
Look under the hood for an ABS sticker.
Look at the tires.
Remove a tire and look for the ABS sensor on the axle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look under the trailer for wheel speed sensors near the back of the brakes.
questions.explanation: To check if a trailer has Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), look under the vehicle for the electronic control unit and wheel speed sensor wires near the back of the brakes.

questions.question: What is true about Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS)?

options.text: They reduce normal braking power.
They work with other braking systems and do not reduce braking power.
They don't work well on larger vehicles.
They are illegal in some states.

questions.correctAnswerText: They work with other braking systems and do not reduce braking power.
questions.explanation: ABS works alongside your normal brakes. It does not increase or decrease braking power. ABS activates during hard braking to keep wheels from locking up.

questions.question: What should you do when leaving your vehicle parked?

options.text: Use the parking brake.
Use the parking brake only if parked on a slope.
Don't use the parking brake because it can damage tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the parking brake.
questions.explanation: Always use the parking brake when you park. However, do not use it if your brakes are very hot or if they are wet and it is freezing.

questions.question: What does the air compressor governor control?

options.text: When air is pumped into the air storage tanks.
How fast air is pumped into the air storage tanks.
The temperature of the air in the storage tanks.
The vehicle's speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: When air is pumped into the air storage tanks.
questions.explanation: In an air brake system, the governor controls when the air compressor pumps air into the storage tanks.
